title: Focus the dialog element instead of the first focusable item

labels.name: needs implementer interest
labels.description: Moving the issue forward requires implementers to express interest

body: This is an attempt to address #1929, based on what seemed to be the most agreeable solution in the comment thread there (despite diverging quite significantly from the originally proposed solution in #2197). This mirrors the change to the W3C HTML spec: https://github.com/w3c/html/pull/1331 (from issue https://github.com/w3c/html/issues/773, which ironically points back to #1929 here as evidence of consensus). To recap the relevant discussion in #1929: 1. @stevefaulkner [raises an accessibility concern about the existing dialog focusing steps](https://github.com/whatwg/html/issues/1929#issuecomment-269790518) > default focus on a control when a dialog is displayed is poor UX and AX in cases where the dialog contains more than a short message and an OK button. In a [follow up comment](https://github.com/whatwg/html/issues/1929#issuecomment-270117755) he states: > I suggest that instead of implementing a flag to override default focus on a control, change the spec so the `dialog` is focusable by default. 2. @MarcoZehe (Mozilla) [adds his support](https://github.com/whatwg/html/issues/1929#issuecomment-272130574): > I would also like to add my support for @stevefaulkner's and @danbeam's proposal to make the dialog focusable by default 3. @cookiecrook (Apple) [clarifies past discussion and adds his support](https://github.com/whatwg/html/issues/1929#issuecomment-272527090) > As the person who was quoted, I should clarify the context. At the time, `` did not receive any focus notifications in any context. It was clear that the API as written would be inaccessible for years to come. We were offering any compromise in the hope that the WHATWG editors would not forego accessibility as a requirement. > > Since that time, Steve and others have pointed out the negative consequences that focusing the first control would have on screen reader and mainstream users alike. I acknowledge those points and retract that initial proposal. > > I've now come around to the proposal of 1. autofocus if applied. 2. otherwise focus the dialog itself. the `` element should be focusable by default There was some statements of support from people on the Chrome team at Google, but it sounds like they are no longer involved in the project. There was hesitancy to make this change, given [long history](https://www.w3.org/Bugs/Public/show_bug.cgi?id=23366) on this topic, but it doesn't sound like there's anyone defending those historic decisions (and in the case of Apple, @cookiecrook is explicitly retracting support). Can we get consensus around this solution? *** /acknowledgements.html ( diff ) /interactive-elements.html ( diff )
